thread:
ashley_ml: Heads up — CI evals started flaking on the new quantized-1.2 bring-up. Seeing duplicate sample counts and spikes in per-shard runtime.
devon_eng: Seen that too. Any pattern on which shard or worker? Could be a retry loop or heartbeat issue.
ashley_ml: Mostly when we run the full suite with 64 workers. Logs show shards being re-assigned mid-run. Example snippet from eval-runner.log:

```
I0316 12:10:01.123 eval_runner] assigned shard=17 -> worker=worker-9
I0316 12:10:07.456 watchdog] missed heartbeat from worker-9 (last=6s)
I0316 12:10:07.457 controller] rescheduling shard=17 -> worker=worker-12
I0316 12:10:07.458 worker-9] still processing seq=1245
I0316 12:10:07.459 controller] duplicate assignment detected: shard=17 active on worker-9 and worker-12
```

ashley_ml: That duplicate assignment results in the same samples being counted twice in the aggregator.
sam_infra: Hmm. Missed heartbeat after 6s sounds like a low threshold. What's the watchdog config in prod vs CI?
devon_eng: CI uses watchdog.timeout=6s, heartbeat.interval=2s by default. On noisy CI hosts a GC pause or proctoring job can cause a missed heartbeat. We should make movement of shards atomic — we currently mark shard as 'IN_PROGRESS' and then clear on handoff which leaves a small window.
maria_sre: Also saw network jitter on that Jenkins pool last week. We shouldn't rely purely on heartbeats. Can we make controller check worker liveliness AND ask for explicit handoff ack before reassigning?
ashley_ml: Proposed patch: when controller wants to reassign, send `RESERVE` to target AND `REQUEST_CANCEL` to old worker, then wait for either `CANCEL_ACK` or `RESERVE_NACK` before marking new assignment active. Fallback after 15s to force kill.
devon_eng: Sounds reasonable. Quick hack could also be: increment a shard assignment version and only accept outputs if version matches. That prevents double-counting without changing flow.
sam_infra: Versioned assignments + idempotent aggregator are good. Aggregator can dedupe by (shard_id, assignment_version, sample_id). What's cost of storing those IDs for entire run?
ashley_ml: We only need to store per-shard last-seen assignment_version and a recent sample hash window. For long runs keep a bloom filter per shard; memory cheap.
maria_sre: For CI immediate fix: bump watchdog.timeout to 20s and heartbeat.interval to 5s on jenkins runs. For prod we should land versioned assignments + cancel/ack protocol.
devon_eng: I'll open a PR with assignment_version + aggregator idempotency tests. Will add unit test that simulates worker pause and duplicate messages.
ci-bot: CI check queued for branch "devon/shard-versioning" — running eval harness unit tests.
ashley_ml: Thanks. Also add a tiny e2e that runs with 8 workers & induced sleeps to catch race.
devon_eng: Yep will add. Assigning to @sam_infra for CI config change and @maria_sre for monitoring alert tweak.
sam_infra: Got it. I'll patch the jenkins template and post the change here when done.
maria_sre: I'll add an alert rule: if reschedule_rate > 0.5% over 5m trigger pager-1, and add a dashboard panel for assignment_version churn.
ashley_ml: Great — keeping this under test will prevent future flakiness. Thanks all :thumbsup:
